headword: {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}

definitions.explanation: Japan's basic public pension system that covers all residents aged 20-59. It is the first tier of Japan's pension system and provides a basic old-age pension.

examples.japanese: {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}に{加入|かにゅう}する。
examples.english: To enroll in the national pension.

examples.japanese: {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}の{保険料|ほけんりょう}は{毎月|まいつき}{払|はら}う。
examples.english: National pension premiums are paid every month.

examples.japanese: 20{歳|さい}になったら{国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}に{入|はい}らなければならない。
examples.english: You must join the national pension when you turn 20.

notes:
Japan's basic pension system covering all residents between ages 20 and 59, including foreign residents. Enrollment is mandatory. Self-employed individuals and students pay premiums directly, while company employees have their contributions handled through {厚生|こうせい}{年金|ねんきん} (employees' pension), which includes the national pension.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}に{加入|かにゅう}する: to enroll in the national pension
- {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}の{保険料|ほけんりょう}: national pension premium
- {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}を{受|う}け{取|と}る: to receive national pension benefits
- {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん}の{免除|めんじょ}: national pension exemption

JAPAN'S PENSION SYSTEM:
- {国民|こくみん}{年金|ねんきん} (1st tier): basic pension for all residents
- {厚生|こうせい}{年金|ねんきん} (2nd tier): employees' pension — additional pension for company employees and civil servants

PRACTICAL NOTE:
Foreign residents who leave Japan after paying into the system for less than 10 years may apply for a {脱退|だったい}{一時金|いちじきん} (lump-sum withdrawal payment).
